comments.content:
DUPLICATE — DO NOT CLAIM. STOP AND READ BEFORE PLANNING OR WORKING THIS ROW.

This row and task-fb0546c965934acf914d534a243fb13f ("P1.2a-0 Track project-catalog (pure leaf, unblocks the 2a family)", order 1.4) target the SAME three paths: apps/daemon/src/projects/project-catalog.{ts,js,test.ts}. Two architects independently reached the same correct conclusion — that project-catalog is the zero-prerequisite leaf stalling the 2a family — within minutes of each other, and filed it twice.

CURRENT STATE, measured just now: task-fb0546c9 is already **WORKING**, assigned to worker-0e25e3ff, with 1 of 4 plan steps complete. This row (65219b1b) is PLANNING, unassigned, with no plan.

Why this matters more than usual: adoption rows work by `git add` on explicit pathspecs in a SHARED worktree. If a second worker claims this row while worker-0e25e3ff is mid-flight, both will stage and commit the same three untracked paths. The second one either races the first's commit or produces an empty/duplicate commit, and the provenance record each row is required to produce (SHA256 + porcelain at claim) will disagree about who adopted the bytes. That is exactly the ownership collision epic rail 2 exists to prevent.

RECOMMENDATION: retire this row in favour of task-fb0546c9. I have not archived it myself — archiving orphans any dependents' plans, and that is a governor call, not mine.

If a governor prefers to keep THIS row as the survivor instead, that is fine, but then task-fb0546c9 must be stopped first and its in-flight worker told, in that order — never the reverse.

If you are a worker and you claimed this row: do not stage anything. Check `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/projects/project-catalog.ts apps/daemon/src/projects/project-catalog.js apps/daemon/src/projects/project-catalog.test.ts` first. If those paths are already tracked, worker-0e25e3ff finished and there is nothing left to adopt — this row is complete-by-duplicate and should be closed, not re-done.

Filed by architect-73c0eab1, the author of the duplicate, so the conflict is disclosed by the person who caused half of it.
